ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2023-01-15
Provider: Dr. Marcus Johnson, MD
Department: Emergency Medicine
Visit Type: ed

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Intermittent heaviness in his left groin

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
The patient returns for evaluation three years after prior presentation with left scrotal discomfort and a 'bag of worms' sensation, now presenting with a 5-month history of intermittent heaviness in his left groin. The discomfort worsens after prolonged standing and during physical exertion. He reports no history of trauma to the area and no recent febrile illness.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- Varicocele (diagnosed 2020-01-15)

MEDICATIONS:
He does not take any medications

ALLERGIES:
No known drug allergies

FAMILY HISTORY:
- Father with lung cancer at age 52
- Paternal grandfather with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
- Mother with hypothyroidism

SOCIAL HISTORY:
He works as a warehouse loader and frequently lifts heavy boxes.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS:
He has not noticed any change in urinary frequency, dysuria, or hematuria.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
Physical examination reveals a soft, compressible mass above the left testis that increases in size when the patient is standing. On palpation, the left testis has an irregular, tortuous texture described as feeling like a “bag of worms.” The right side of the scrotum appears normal. Abdominal examination is unremarkable with no palpable masses or organomegaly. There is no peripheral edema or cyanosis.

attachments.text:
ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2020-01-15
Provider: Dr. Sarah Chen, MD
Department: Urology
Visit Type: outpatient

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Discomfort and a 'bag of worms' sensation in his left scrotum

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
He presents to the clinic with a 6-month history of discomfort and a "bag of worms" sensation in his left scrotum. The discomfort is mild, described as a dull ache that worsens with prolonged standing and improves when lying down. He denies any trauma, fever, dysuria, or discharge.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
His past medical history is unremarkable

MEDICATIONS:
He takes no medications

ALLERGIES:
No known drug allergies

FAMILY HISTORY:
- Father with lung cancer at age 52
- Paternal grandfather with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
- Mother with hypothyroidism

SOCIAL HISTORY:
Smoking: Current smoker, 1 pack per day for 10 years. Alcohol: Occasional, 1-2 drinks per week. Occupation: Warehouse loader.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
On physical examination, an irregular mass is palpated above the left testicle that increases in size with Valsalva maneuvers. The mass does not transilluminate. The remainder of the examination is normal.

IMAGING:
Testicular ultrasound shows dilated veins within the pampiniform plexus with reversal of flow during the Valsalva maneuver.
